input: Please use the space below to describe the reasons you want to be a solicitor. Outline what first prompted your interest in the profession, your research on the profession, and particular areas of law that interest you. (300 words)
output:
I want to practise as a solicitor because I am drawn to the way legal work can protect people and influence how communities function. That curiosity began at school: debates and mock trials were my first contact with structured advocacy, and the discipline of building an argument under pressure made a legal career feel both challenging and purposeful.

Later research and experience clarified what solicitors actually do. Panel discussions with practitioners, including sessions hosted by [redacted], showed how solicitors untangle difficult problems while investing in lasting client relationships. An internship with [redacted] then made that concrete in family law: supporting work on divorce matters and financial settlements demonstrated the real consequences of careful advice for clients at vulnerable moments, and confirmed that this is the path I want.

Within that path I am especially interested in family law and art law, each demanding both analysis and people skills. Family work attracts me for its human stakes and the chance to guide clients through emotionally charged change. Art law appeals because it sits where creativity meets commerce—protecting intellectual property, handling disputes, and advising on high-value deals. Studying intellectual property law this year has sharpened that interest and shown how quickly the area evolves.

Becoming a solicitor therefore combines the problem-solving I enjoy with the chance to make a practical difference. I aim to build the technical depth, flexibility, and interpersonal judgement the role requires, and to contribute in practice areas that are both intellectually lively and centred on people.
